title: Fantasy Player News
description: Breaking Fantasy Football player news along with the impact for fantasy managers

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Puka Nacua (hip) inactive for Week 2
items.desc: Puka Nacua (hip) is officially inactive for Week 2 for the Los Angeles Rams against the New York Giants according to Adam Schefter.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Zach Ertz returning to Eagles
items.desc: The Eagles signed TE Zach Ertz to their practice squad.
items.impact: Philadelphia brings back an old friend in Ertz with Dallas Goedert expected to miss a few weeks with an MCL sprain. Ertz could be brought up from the practice squad next week.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Cobie Durant (hamstring) could miss a few weeks
items.desc: Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer said Cobie Durant could miss a few weeks.
items.impact: Durant went down with a hamstring injury in Sunday's game against the Commanders. He is week-to-week for now.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: P.J. Locke (foot) could miss a few weeks
items.desc: Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer said P.J. Locke could miss a few weeks.
items.impact: Locke went down with a foot injury in Sunday's game against the Commanders. He is week-to-week for now.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: DeMarvion Overshown (hamstring) 'making progress'
items.desc: Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer said DeMarvion Overshown is making progress from his hamstring injury.
items.impact: Schottenheimer added that he is not sure if Overshown will be able to play this coming Sunday.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Charlie Kolar (forearm) placed on IR
items.desc: The Chargers placed TE Charlie Kolar on injured reserve.
items.impact: Kolar suffered the injury in Sunday's game against the Raiders. With David Njoku also on IR, Oronde Gadsden is the only healthy tight end on the Chargers right now.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: David Njoku (knee) placed on IR
items.desc: The Chargers placed TE David Njoku on injured reserve.
items.impact: Njoku was carted off the field in Sunday's game against the Raiders. With Charlie Kolar (forearm) also placed on IR, Oronde Gadsden is the only healthy tight end on the Chargers right now.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Dallas Goedert suffers MCL sprain, to miss a few weeks
items.desc: Dallas Goedert suffered a sprained MCL in Sunday's win over the Titans.
items.impact: The injury is expected to sideline Goedert for at least a few weeks. DeVonta Smith, Dontayvion Wicks and Makai Lemon should all step up even more in the passing game for Jalen Hurts.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Mykel Williams (knee) will not return to practice this week
items.desc: 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan said Mykel Williams is being held out of practice until next week.
items.impact: Williams opened the season on the PUP list. He is working his way back from a torn ACL.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Romello Height suffers broken hand, to require surgery
items.desc: 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan said Romello Height broke his hand and will need surgery.
items.impact: Shanahan added there's still a possibility he will play on Sunday.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Jaylen Wright (neck/shoulder) day-to-day
items.desc: Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said Jaylen Wright is day-to-day.
items.impact: Wright left Sunday's game early with a neck/shoulder injury.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Caleb Douglas dealing with ankle injury
items.desc: Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said it's "too early to tell" at this point on WR Caleb Douglas with his ankle.
items.impact: Douglas will need to be monitored in practice this week for his ankle injury.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: James Thompson Jr. suffers ankle sprain
items.desc: 49ers DT James Thompson Jr. suffered a high-ankle sprain in Sunday's game against the Dolphins.
items.impact: Thompson will likely miss some time with the injury.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Demarcus Robinson (ankle) could be placed on IR
items.desc: Demarcus Robinson is a candidate to be placed on IR after suffering a high-ankle sprain on Sunday against the Dolphins.
items.impact: Robinson would be forced to miss at least four games if he is placed on IR.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Mike Evans to manage hip injury this week
items.desc: 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan said Mike Evans' hip injury will have to be managed this week.
items.impact: Evans exited Sunday's 35-13 victory over the Dolphins in the second half and did not return. His status will need to be monitored in practice this week.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Alec Pierce (heel) to seek second opinion
items.desc: Colts WR Alec Pierce is expected to seek a second opinion on his heel injury.
items.impact: Pierce had X-rays return negative on his injury on Sunday. Head coach Shane Steichen said the team is "still gathering information" after Pierce aggravated his surgically repaired left heel in Sunday's game against the Chiefs.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Michael Penix Jr. (knee) named starting quarterback for Week 3
items.desc: Michael Penix Jr. (knee) has been named the starting quarterback for Week 3 for the Atlanta Falcons according to Ian Rapoport.
items.impact: Penix Jr. will take over behind center after missing the first two contests while continuing to work back from a serious knee injury suffered last season, with Cooper Rush leading an underwhelming Atlanta offense to two losses. The signal-caller should provide a boost to playmakers Bijan Robinson and Drake London moving forward, although fantasy manager may want to temper expectations against a strong Green Bay defense Thursday night.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Nick Cross being evaluated for 'internal injury'
items.desc: Commanders head coach Dan Quinn said S Nick Cross spent the night in the hospital on Sunday night due to an "internal injury" he suffered in Sunday's game against the Cowboys.
items.impact: Cross was discharged from the hospital on Monday. His status is up in the air heading into Week 3 against the Seahawks.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Jayden Reed still being evaluated for back injury
items.desc: The Packers are "still evaluating" the treatment and recovery timeframe for Jayden Reed after his injury in Week 2.
items.impact: Schefter notes it was a back injury for Reed on Sunday after it was originally reported to be a neck injury. Christian Watson, Matthew Golden, and Tucker Kraft should all see expanded roles for as long as he is sidelined.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) uncertain for Week 3
items.desc: Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy said he is unsure if Michael Pittman will play in Week 3 against the Bengals.
items.impact: Pittman was sidelined on Sunday with a foot injury he is still working his way back from. Germie Bernard went on to see an expanded role in his absence.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Jauan Jennings (personal) expected to return for Week 3
items.desc: Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell said Jauan Jennings is expected to return for Week 3.
items.impact: Jennings did not play on Sunday due to personal reasons. He was targeted just once in Week 1. He's off the fantasy radar for now.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Aaron Jones Sr. 'pretty sore' after Week 2
items.desc: Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell said Aaron Jones was "pretty sore" after Minnesota's Week 2 win against the Bears.
items.impact: Jones led the backfield on Sunday with Jordan Mason on injured reserve. DeeJay Dallas and Demond Claiborne are the current backups behind Jones. Jones will need to be monitored in practice this week.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Treydan Stukes in concussion protocol
items.desc: The Raiders placed DB Treydan Stukes in concussion protocol.
items.impact: The status of Stukes is up in the air heading into Week 3.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Brock Bowers (knee) will practice this week
items.desc: Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak said Brock Bowers will practice this week.
items.impact: Bowers returned to a limited practice last Friday. His status will need to be monitored in practice this week as he hopes to return in Week 3 against the Saints.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Marcus Mariota expected to start at quarterback in Week 3
items.desc: Marcus Mariota is expected to start at quarterback for the Washington Commanders in Week 3 according to Adam Schefter.
items.impact: Mariota will once again be tasked with stepping behind center for head coach Dan Quinn after Jayden Daniels (elbow) went down in a Week 2 loss to the Dallas Cowboys, facing a Seattle Seahawks defense that has been disruptive once again to begin they season.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Jayden Daniels (elbow) undergoes imaging Monday
items.desc: Jayden Daniels underwent imaging on his dislocated elbow on Monday.
items.impact: Daniels is now slated to consult with a variety of experts over the next few days. He remains without a clear timetable to return.

items.author: Jesse Garcia
items.title: Tyler Loop makes one field goal in Week 2 loss
items.desc: Tyler Loop made 1-of-2 field goals and 2-of-2 extra point attempts in the Ravens loss to the Saints.
items.impact: Loop had a 49-yard field goal blocked in the first half, but made a 49-yard field goal in the second half. The Ravens take on the Cowboys in Week 3, which should provide Loop with plenty of chances in what should be a high scoring matchup.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Kyler Murray clears concussion protocol, will start Week 3
items.desc: Kyler Murray has cleared concussion protocol and will start against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday.
items.impact: Murray missed the Vikings Week 2 slog of a win over the Bears, but he will be back in the lineup for Week 3 against a hapless Tampa defense. Murray is still a bit of an unknown at this point given he barely played in Week 1, but this is a perfect matchup to return to.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Chad Ryland quiet in loss to Seattle
items.desc: Chad Ryland hit his only PAT in the Cardinals' 31-7 loss to the Seahawks on Sunday.
items.impact: It was a quiet day for the Cardinals kicker, who didn't even get to attempt a field goal the whole game. Better days will come for him, but he's tough to trust for fantasy.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Arizona Cardinals D/ST run over by Seattle offense in Week 2
items.desc: The Arizona Cardinals D/ST was completely outmatched against the Seattle Seahawks offensive attack, losing 34-3 in the process. The unit managed just one sack and a fumble recovery.
items.impact: After a half-decent showing against the Chargers, the Cardinals defense was put back in their place by the much better run Seattle offense. Arizona's lack of talent on the defensive side of the ball screams that they should be well off of streaming radar, and that was evident on Sunday.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Kelvin Banks Jr. (ankle sprain) to undergo surgery, out indefinitely
items.desc: Saints OT Kelvin Banks Jr. suffered a severe high-ankle sprain and is now expected to have surgery to repair it.
items.impact: Banks will be sidelined indefinitely. He has a chance to return late in the season if all goes well.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Emmett Johnson expected to continue to see more snaps
items.desc: Chiefs head coach Andy Reid said Emmett Johnson will continue to get more and more snaps.
items.impact: Reid added that Johnson will see more snaps and take some of the workload off of Kenneth Walker. The rookie has flashed in a limited role over the first two weeks of the season. He remains a solid stash for fantasy managers in his current role.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Patrick Jones II (back) hopeful to return in Week 3
items.desc: Panthers coach Dave Canales said he optimistic about LB Pat Jones potentially returning this week at Cleveland.
items.impact: Jones missed the first two games of the season with a back injury.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Josh Simmons (back) without clear update on return
items.desc: Chiefs head coach Andy Reid said the team anticipated Josh Simmons would miss "two, three, four games."
items.impact: Reid said Simmons has been doing 'everything' behind the scenes. The Chiefs want to make sure his swelling is down.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Mansoor Delane (shoulder) trending in right direction
items.desc: Chiefs head coach Andy Reid said Mansoor Delane could have played if needed on Sunday.
items.impact: Reid added that they wanted to give Delane some more time to heal if possible. His status will be worth monitoring in practice this week.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Jadarian Price suffers shoulder injury Sunday
items.desc: Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said Jadarian Price suffered a shoulder injury in Sunday's win against the Cardinals.
items.impact: It was originally reported to be a chest injury for Price, but Macdonald said Monday it was a shoulder injury. He  said "it's intact and nothing serious, it seems like." Emmanuel Wilson wound up seeing 21 carries. He would figure to see a big role in Week 3 against the Commanders if Price is sidelined.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Jonathon Brooks (groin) undergoing tests
items.desc: Panthers head coach Dave Canales said RB Jonathon Brooks is undergoing tests on his groin injury.
items.impact: The team is still gathering information on the severity of the injury. There should be an update on Brooks this week.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Nico Collins (hamstring) uncertain for Week 3
items.desc: Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans did not have an update on Nico Collins' hamstring injury.
items.impact: Wilson noted that according to a source, Collins is currently not expected to play in Week 3 against the Colts. If he remains sidelined, Dalton Schultz will remain a TE1 with Xavier Hutchinson, Kayshon Boutte, and Jaylin Noel also all seeing expanded roles.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: J.K. Dobbins (hamstring) avoids major injury
items.desc: J.K. Dobbins is reportedly "good" after injuring his hamstring in Sunday's game against the Jaguars.
items.impact: Dobbins was unable to finish Sunday's win over Jacksonville. His status will need to be monitored in practice this week. Rookie RB Jonah Coleman took over the backfield to finish Sunday's game RJ Harvey (hamstring) sidelined.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Drew Lock leans on JSN in win over Cardinals
items.desc: Drew Lock completed 19 of 26 passes for 235 yards and three touchdowns in the Seahawks' 31-7 win over the Cardinals.
items.impact: 155 of his passing yards and all of his touchdowns went to Jaxon Smith-Njigba. Lock was thrust into the starting role because of Sam Darnold's injury, but through most of two weeks, he's been just fine and has leaned on his superstar wideout to do most of the work for him. If he starts again, he gets a nice matchup against the Commanders' struggling defense.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Jaxon Smith-Njigba has hat trick of touchdowns in win
items.desc: Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught 9 of 11 targets for 155 yards and three touchdowns in the Seahawks' 31-7 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
items.impact: JSN has been on an absolute tear to start the season, with 277 yards through the first two games. He's looking QB-proof at the moment, and as long as Drew Lock can continue to get him the ball with Sam Darnold still out, JSN is an auto start. Not that you were sitting him anyway. He gets a great matchup against the Commanders next week.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Caleb Williams (hamstring) labeled week-to-week with hamstring injury
items.desc: Caleb Williams (hamstring) is "week-to-week", per HC Ben Johnson. Initial optimism about his status has given way to reality, and it now seems likely Williams will miss time.
items.impact: It's a bummer for Williams, who looked to be on his way to a great start to the year. Tyson Bagent is the next man up in Chicago, and he's shown promise in previous outings when taking over for Williams.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Colts D/ST struggles in overtime loss Sunday
items.desc: The Colts' D/ST logged two sacks and allowed 33 points in Sunday night's overtime loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.
items.impact: Indianapolis' defense looked bad for a second-straight week on Sunday night. They weren't able to force a single turnover against the Chiefs and ended up allowing 33 points over the course of the night, which was enough to give Kansas City the win in overtime. This unit should not be played in most fantasy leagues for the foreseeable future, even in more favorable matchups.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Spencer Shrader perfect in overtime loss Sunday
items.desc: Spencer Shrader went 3-for-3 on his field-goal attempts and 3-for-3 on his extra-point attempts in Sunday night's 33-30 overtime loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.
items.impact: Shrader did his job on Sunday night. He made all six of his kicks against the Chiefs, which left him with 12 points over the course of the night. That wasn't enough for Indianapolis to pick up the win in overtime, however, as they now drop to 0-2 on the season.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Laquon Treadwell racks up 61 yards Sunday
items.desc: Laquon Treadwell caught three passes for 61 yards in Sunday night's 33-30 OT loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.
items.impact: The veteran stepped up on Sunday after Alec Pierce left the game due to a heel injury. Treadwell played well and racked up 61 yards on the night, though he still wasn't great from a fantasy perspective. He should be more involved moving forward but still shouldn't be rostered in most league formats.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Avonte Maddox (foot) out for season with foot injury
items.desc: Avonte Maddox (foot) will require season-ending foot surgery to repair the injury he sustained against the Bills on Thursday.
items.impact: It's a tough break for Maddox and the Detroit defense, who lose yet another veteran in what is already a struggling defense. They'll have to bring in some new names and hope for the best in their defensive backfield.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Keenan Allen held to one catch Sunday
items.desc: Keenan Allen caught 1-of-5 targets for just five yards in Sunday's 33-30 overtime loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.
items.impact: The veteran saw five opportunities on Sunday night, but he was only able to haul in one catch for five yards over the course of the night. He hasn't looked very good over the first two games of the season, which mitigates a lot of the optimism surrounding him now that Alec Pierce (heel) seems set to miss time.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Josh Downs leads team in receiving Sunday
items.desc: Josh Downs hauled in 7-of-9 targets for 72 yards in Sunday night's 33-30 overtime loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.
items.impact: The Colts needed Downs to step up on Sunday night, and he did just that, delivering a team-high 72 yards in a narrow loss to the Chiefs. He seems primed to improve as a fantasy option in the near future with Alec Pierce (heel) seemingly set to miss some time after aggravating an injury.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Tyler Warren hauls in touchdown Sunday
items.desc: Tyler Warren hauled in 6-of-7 targets for 21 yards and a touchdown in Sunday night's 33-30 overtime loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.
items.impact: The young tight end had an up-and-down night on Sunday. On one hand, he finished with a touchdown and six catches on the night, which led to good results in PPR leagues. On the other hand, he only totaled 21 yards on his seven targets, which is poor as far as efficiency goes. Fantasy managers should continue to expect high volume from him moving forward, especially with Alec Pierce (heel) seemingly set to miss some time.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Daniel Jones solid in overtime loss Sunday
items.desc: Daniel Jones completed 22-of-31 passing attempts for 210 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in Sunday night's 33-30 overtime loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.
items.impact: Jones didn't have a spectacular showing on Sunday night, but he was pretty solid and limited mistakes for Indianapolis' offense. That was almost enough for them to pick up a road win over Kansas City, but they ended up narrowly losing in overtime. The veteran quarterback shouldn't be rostered in most league formats at this point.
